Commentary.Commentary: We are back. The players are out in the middle. Kusal Mendis and Pathum Nissanka to open. Mitchell Santner to bowl first.
...THE CHASE...

Can't really write a lot about the Kiwi's batting line up. Most of the batters scored in single figures. There were a couple who got over 20 but they could not kick on. New Zealand will need a special effort if they're to defend this. Sri Lanka on the other hand, should chase this down.

That's another fine bowling effort from the hosts! It was Thushara who started it off and then Hasaranga tormented the Kiwis. He was the pick but it was an overall effort from the hosts. Just what their captain would have wanted after electing to bowl.

So, will the Black Caps rebound to prevent a clean sweep, or will the Sri Lankan team secure their second consecutive victory? Join us for an engaging match filled with anticipation and excitement! Toss and team news to follow shortly...

Led by Charith Asalanka, the Lankans will aim to secure the series, while Mitchell Santner's New Zealand will seek redemption after a disappointing batting display in the first match. With both teams looking to make necessary adjustments, fans can expect an action-packed encounter.

Welcome to the thrilling second and final T20I between Sri Lanka and New Zealand at Rangiri Dambulla International Stadium! After a nail-biting opener where Sri Lanka clinched victory by four wickets, the stage is set for an exciting decider.
... Match Day ...

As we turn our attention to the 2nd T20I of the New Zealand tour of Sri Lanka, the stakes are clear. Sri Lanka, buoyed by their recent triumph in the series opener, will be eager to solidify their standing with a second consecutive victory, which would seal the series in their favor. The hosts demonstrated remarkable resilience and skill in Dambulla, successfully chasing down a target of 135 with four wickets in hand. In that gripping first encounter, New Zealand elected to bat first after winning the toss, a decision that initially seemed promising. However, they found themselves under pressure as Sri Lankan bowlers, led by the impressive Dunith Wellalage, dismantled the Kiwi batting order with precision. The Sri Lankan chase began on a shaky note but the partnership between Pathum Nissanka and Kusal Perera revived their hopes. Later, it was the calm presence of skipper Charith Asalanka that truly steadied the ship, as he forged a critical partnership with Wanindu Hasaranga to guide the chase. Foulkes stood out for the Kiwis with the bat and the ball, as he scored a quickfire 27 at the end for them and finished with commendable figures of 3 for 20. Expect an enticing contest, with both sides having much to play for as they step onto the field.
